title: June 7th, State of the People Power Tour: Co-Hosted by the Social Justice Learning Institute (SJLI)
description:
We’re excited to invite you to volunteer with SJLI to co-host the State of the People POWER Tour Los Angeles Stop. 

This day of the tour is happening June 7th in Alta Dena, California.

This experience is more than an event—it’s a movement for healing, truth-telling, and transformation. Together, we’ll build collective power through joy, culture, and action.

🖤 Here’s what you can expect:

This day of the tour occurs in Altadena, and focuses on:

Community Healing Circles addressing the impacts of recent events like the Eaton Fire.

Field Hearings where residents can voice concerns and propose solutions.

Youth Engagement Sessions empowering the next generation of leaders.

A Closing Ceremony celebrating our collective resilience and outlining next steps for sustained action.

This event is organized by a coalition of dedicated organizations, including Black Power Network, BlackPAC, LeadersUp, and the Social Justice Learning Institute, committed to building a lasting Black power ecosystem.

We look forward to your participation in this transformative experience!

All registered volunteers will be contacted upon signing up via whatever email and/or phone number used to register!

title: NO KINGS! March

address_lines: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details
location.venue: This event’s address is private. Sign up for more details

description:
On June 14—Flag Day—Donald Trump wants tanks in the street and a made-for-TV display of dominance for his birthday. A spectacle meant to look like strength. But real power isn’t staged in Washington. It rises up everywhere else.

No Kings is a nationwide day of defiance. From city blocks to small towns, from courthouse steps to community parks, we’re taking action to reject authoritarianism—and show the world what democracy really looks like.

We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.

The flag doesn’t belong to Donald Trump. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.

On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.

Ours is a gateway community, and Trump seeks to capture and deport immigrants -- both undocumented and legal -- to enhance and display his power.  He also seeks to destroy -- not improve -- our federal workforce.  One-third of that workforce is made up of military veterans.  Those veterans and their coworkers work for all of us!  Therefore we march also on behalf of veterans in front of the Veterans Administration medical campus in Brockton.

This event is organized by Brockton Indivisible.
accessibility_notes: Those unable to march the half mile can bring walkers or outdoor chairs and set up on the sidewalk in front of the VA by noon.

title: New Member Orientation! (Summer Series)
description:
As a member-led youth movement, MOVE Texas Members are at the heart of our mission to transform democracy in Texas and beyond. **Born out of the student organizing movement in San Antonio in 2013,** MOVE Texas was founded by young people who saw a gap in civic engagement and decided to take action. What started as a small group of student leaders registering their peers to vote has since grown into a statewide movement of young people that trains, mobilizes, and empowers a new generation of progressive community organizers.

## Who are MOVE Texas Members?

MOVE Texas members are the backbone of the organization, reflecting the energy and diversity of young Texans leading the charge for a more just and equitable future for all Texans across race, class, and place.  As a youth movement, MOVE Texas members are under 30, and are either:


- **Students:** The original foundation of MOVE Texas—young leaders organizing on campuses across the state, running voter registration drives, educating their peers, and leading local issue-based campaigns.

- **Community Members:** Young Texans who are inspired by MOVE Texas’ mission and actively work to build power in their neighborhoods, from hosting events to advocating for direct local and statewide policy change.

## MOVE Texas members receive:

- Access to MOVE trainings, programs, and resources,

- Voting power for statewide and local campaigns,

- Exclusive invitations to MOVE statewide events,

- Connection to a network of peers organizing across the state,

- Exclusive members merch.


MOVE Texas membership is open to anyone who believes in the power of young people to lead and shape the future AND our present. **By becoming a member, you’re not just supporting a movement—you are the movement.**

title: Support an Ethical Democracy!
description:
Join other FVWA democracy champions on Tuesday, June 3rd to give public testimony and let the Seattle City Council know that we want to maintain an ethical, accountable government! 

On Thursday May 8, the Governance Accountability and Economic Development Committee heard legislation that would change the Code of Ethics to allow for Councilmembers to be able to vote on legislation even if they have a financial interest. 

**Since the legislation was introduced, the City Council has received hundreds of emails from neighbors voicing their concerns about the implications of this.**

FVWA staff and supporters, as well as other democracy supporting orgs will be meeting in the Lobby of City Hall around 1:30pm and heading up to the Council room around 1:45pm to sign up for testimony. 

**This is an important opportunity to show up and support Washington state, and Seattle specifically, as the standard-bearers of transparent, accessible democracy! Join us!**



*Learn more about what to expect from public comment and testimony HERE: https://www.seattle.gov/council/committees/public-comment*
